page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at top right, page number at top left. Under the head, a centred title, three short centred small-caps subtitles and four verse passages. A catchword at lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: E GRÆCO SIMONIDIS.
main_text.p: Homo cūm sis nihil affere [?] stabile: Nec ubi videris hominem, certa Spatia ætatis promitte: etenim Musca volucris res in morem Inconstantia rotat humanas.
main_text.head: EX EODEM.
main_text.p: Nec ullus expers criminis nec mortis est.
main_text.head: EX EODEM.
main_text.p: Ut arma fugias fata non fugies tamen.
main_text.head: EX EODEM.
main_text.p: De luce caßis cor memoriam non supra Unum tenebit, si cor habeamus, diem.
main_text.head: IN BELEAGONEM.
main_text.p: Ei quem parentis colere debueras loco, Beleago, vino spolia detrahere cupis, Quod tu capella non facis nisi mortua. Lanium sciebant esse te cuncti[?] gradum Ut carnifex sis, inde paulatim facis: Ne quæstus[?] ullus non lucrum ferat tibi. Ut carnifex sis artis auspicium tamen Aliunde malim feceris. Visne ut tibi Dicam unde possis optime, ut si etiam parum Ex arte facias, nil tamen peccaueris. Suspende te ipse: etsi imperite id feceris Omnes probabunt ceu foret factum[?] optime.

page.notes: Line 1: the word "affere" is read as "affere"; the first letters are doubtful. "nihil" is printed with a Greek-looking eta; I read it as nihil. The mark before "Musca" (line 4) is a printed symbol, not a letter. "cuncti" (line 3 of the Beleagon poem) looks like a printing error, possibly "cunctli" as printed. "quæstus" and "factum" are doubtful. The first poem's paragraph and the catchword "ALIO-" are read from the right edge; the faint show-through text on the right edge is left out.
